send_redirect() emits a fixed 302 Found; there is no API to choose the status, and no header API at all (see the beaker-post row). 303 would be the correct code after a GET-that-writes; 302 is what the library sends. The write handler redirects to a clean URL so a submitted value never sits in history either way.

The raw request buffer (beaker's current_request_buffer thread-local) contains the whole request INCLUDING a POST body and Content-Length. This contradicts the round-6 beaker-post row: beaker does not PARSE a body into UrlParams, but a handler can read it. So a POST form is feasible with a small in-app parser, and secrets need not travel in the URL.

beaker_get_header(name) returns the right value per name (Host, User-Agent, X-First/Second/Third all distinct). One caveat: for a POST with a Content-Type header present on the wire, beaker_get_header("Content-Type") returned an empty string. Read the raw buffer for that.

X3 resolved. The recorded cause was the 2 s page deadline; the real cause was CURLOPT_CONNECTTIMEOUT_MS hardcoded to 700 ms in ScrapingHttp.c. curl measured openlibrary.org's TLS handshake at 1.07-1.41 s over two paced probes, so every request was cut off at 700 ms and logged 'Timeout was reached (http=0)', recorded as SUSPEND_TRANSPORT - 'unreachable' for a host that answers. Raised to 2000 ms.

The whole request PATH is capped at 255 characters (a 254-char path answers 302, a 256-char path 400 'canonicalize_path: Path is too long'). This is the real cause of the owner's HTTP ERROR 400 on 'Save server settings': eight form fields plus a 32-byte nonce exceed it, so the longer a value is, the more certain the failure. GET cannot carry a settings form; a POST body is required, and the raw buffer does contain one (beaker-post-body row).
